safety_lead_time.comparison_action: DECREASE - Recommended safety lead time is lower than SAP

narrative: Demand for PL1__M4716C03 is moderately variable (CV=38%) with a statistically significant downward trend (Mann-Kendall p<0.001) and a right-skewed empirical distribution. Lead times are moderate in stability (CV=37.6%, mean=2.45 days), with transport variability as the dominant source. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy was selected: EOQ drives a large order quantity of 19,490 units to minimise total replenishment and holding costs, while the safety stock of 1,443 units is calibrated to deliver the 95% service level target using combined demand-and-lead-time uncertainty. The current SAP policy over-orders in frequency (MOQ=953 vs EOQ=19,490), creating an ~90% cost inefficiency that can be corrected without any capacity or feasibility constraint.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous and non-zero on all working days with moderate variability. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is well-suited: it triggers a fixed order of economic quantity Q whenever inventory reaches reorder point r, providing responsive replenishment without the overhead of periodic review. EOQ is appropriate because both ordering and holding costs are well-defined and the demand rate is relatively stable.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The order quantity of 19,490 units combined with a safety stock of 1,443 units totals 20,933 units, well within the 44,671-unit storage limit (47% utilisation). No capacity constraint binds. The trend-detected flag warrants monitoring: if demand continues to decline, the EOQ and reorder point should be recalibrated.
